hero.title: Methods
intro.0: A method is a named piece of behaviour: hand it some input, it hands back an answer - the same idea as a check you used to run by hand. The syntax here is small on purpose. The real goal is to feel what a method is for: write a rule once, then reuse it.
task.1.title: A method hands back a result
task.1.context: A method is a named piece of behaviour that gives back an answer. You ran checks like this by hand as a tester - now the code holds the check.
task.1.goal.1: Run it. The output should be `OK`.
task.2.title: Give the method some input
task.2.context: Real checks depend on data. A `parameter` is the value you hand in when you call the method.
task.2.goal.0: Make `Label(int age)` return `"Age: "` followed by the `age`.
task.2.goal.1: `Main` calls `Label(18)`, so the output should be `Age: 18`.
task.3.title: Let the method decide
task.3.context: A method can hold a rule, the way a test holds a pass/fail condition. Same input always gives the same answer.
task.3.goal.0: Return `"adult"` when `age` is 18 or more, otherwise `"minor"`.
task.3.goal.1: `Main` calls `Category(20)`, so the output should be `adult`.
task.4.title: One method, many cases
task.4.context: This is the payoff. You wrote the rule once; now run it against several inputs without repeating yourself.
task.4.goal.1: Call it for ages 16, 18 and 40 and print each result.
task.4.goal.2: The output must be exactly three lines: `minor`, `adult`, `adult`.
task.5.title: A method that uses another method
task.5.context: Methods can call each other, so a bigger answer is just small checks combined. This is the habit every later lesson builds on.
task.5.goal.1: `Main` calls `Summary(20)`, so the output should be `Status: adult`.
